utilities.name: close-session
examples:
Close the current Sandstorm session after app-specific work is complete.
Command: close-session <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: asks Sandstorm to close the current session or tab for that user.
Returns: no output on success.

utilities.name: enter-grain
utilities.summary: Enters a Linux process's namespaces and launches an interactive shell there.
utilities.description: Enter a Sandstorm grain's Linux namespaces and launch a shell there.
examples:
Attach to a running grain process by PID.
Command: enter-grain <pid>
Arguments: <pid> is the process ID of a grain process already running inside Sandstorm.
Effect: joins that process's user, IPC, UTS, network, PID, and mount namespaces, switches to its current working directory, and launches /bin/bash with the target environment.
Returns: an interactive shell session or a non-zero exit status on failure.

utilities.name: get-public-id
utilities.summary: Returns the current grain's public ID metadata.
utilities.description: Fetch the current grain's public ID metadata.
examples:
Fetch the grain's public ID metadata as plain text for logs or shell scripts.
Command: get-public-id <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: newline-delimited text containing the public ID, hostname, auto URL, and demo-user flag.
Use this form when a human or shell pipeline is reading the output.

Fetch the grain's public ID metadata as JSON for programmatic use.
Command: get-public-id --json <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: JSON with publicId, hostname, autoUrl, and isDemoUser.
Use this form when an app or agent needs structured fields.

utilities.name: get-session-offer
utilities.summary: Inspects the Powerbox offer attached to a Sandstorm session.
utilities.description: Inspect the Powerbox offer attached to a Sandstorm session.
examples:
Inspect the Powerbox offer attached to the current session before deciding how to handle an incoming capability.
Command: get-session-offer <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: JSON describing the attached Powerbox offer and any decoded tag payloads.
Use this when an app needs to understand what the user just offered through the Powerbox.

utilities.name: get-session-request
utilities.summary: Inspects the Powerbox request descriptors attached to a Sandstorm session.
utilities.description: Inspect the Powerbox request descriptors attached to a Sandstorm session.
examples:
Inspect the Powerbox request descriptors attached to the current session before deciding what capabilities to offer.
Command: get-session-request <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: JSON describing the request descriptors and any decoded tag payloads.
Use this when an app needs to understand what the user is asking for through the Powerbox.

utilities.name: get-user-address
utilities.summary: Returns the authenticated user's email address and display name.
utilities.description: Fetch the authenticated user's email address and display name.
examples:
Fetch the authenticated user's address as plain text for logs or shell scripts.
Command: get-user-address <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: newline-delimited text containing the email address and display name.
The address may be blank in local development or when Sandstorm does not expose one.

Fetch the authenticated user's address as JSON for programmatic use.
Command: get-user-address --json <sessionId>
Arguments: <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Returns: JSON with address and name.
The address may be blank in local development or when Sandstorm does not expose one.

utilities.name: open-view
utilities.summary: Asks Sandstorm to open a grain-relative path in the current or a new tab.
utilities.description: Ask Sandstorm to open a grain-relative path in the current or a new tab.
examples:
Open a grain-relative path in the current tab.
Command: open-view --path /docs/123 <sessionId>
Arguments: --path is the grain-relative path to open and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: asks Sandstorm to navigate the existing session to that path.
Returns: no output on success.

Open a grain-relative path in a new tab.
Command: open-view --path /docs/123 --new-tab <sessionId>
Arguments: --path is the grain-relative path to open, --new-tab requests a new tab, and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: asks Sandstorm to open that path in a separate browser tab.
Returns: no output on success.

utilities.name: post-activity
utilities.summary: Posts a structured activity event to the current Sandstorm session.
utilities.description: Post a structured activity event to the current Sandstorm session.
examples:
Post a simple activity event using direct flags.
Command: post-activity --path /issues/1#comment-2 --type 3 --thread-path /issues/1 --thread-title "Issue 1" --caption "New comment" <sessionId>
Arguments: --path is the grain-relative activity path, --type is the app-defined event type index, --thread-path and --thread-title identify the thread, --caption sets the notification caption, and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: creates an activity or notification entry visible through Sandstorm.
Returns: no output on success.

Post a richer activity event from JSON when the payload is too large or structured for flags.
Command: post-activity --json-input event.json <sessionId>
Arguments: --json-input points to a JSON file containing the activity payload and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: creates an activity or notification entry using the structured JSON payload.
Returns: no output on success.

utilities.name: send-email
utilities.summary: Sends an email through the current Sandstorm session.
utilities.description: Send an email through the current Sandstorm session.
examples:
Send a plain-text email with direct flags.
Command: send-email --to user@example.com --subject "Hello" --text "Hi there" <sessionId>
Arguments: --to is the recipient address, --subject sets the subject line, --text sets the plain-text body, and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: asks Sandstorm to send the message through the current grain's email capability.
Returns: no output on success.

Send an email from a JSON message definition when the message has more structure.
Command: send-email --json-input message.json <sessionId>
Arguments: --json-input points to a JSON file describing the message and <sessionId> is the Sandstorm session ID for the current request.
Effect: asks Sandstorm to send the structured message from the JSON payload.
Returns: no output on success.

utilities.name: stay-awake
utilities.summary: Keeps a Sandstorm wake lock active for the lifetime of the helper process.
utilities.description: Keep a Sandstorm wake lock active for the lifetime of the helper process.
examples:
Run stay-awake as a child helper while background work is in progress.
Command: stay-awake --title "Transcoding video" --caption "Encoding in the background"
Arguments: --title and --caption control the notification text. Spawn this helper as a subprocess and keep its stdin open while the background task is active.
Lock lifetime: the wake lock stays active until the stay-awake process exits, its stdin is closed, or it receives SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGINT.
Returns: no output on success.

Hold a wake lock for a bounded amount of time.
Command: stay-awake --for 30s --title "Transcoding video" --caption "Encoding in the background"
Arguments: --for sets the maximum time to hold the lock and --title and --caption control the notification text.
Lock lifetime: the wake lock is released when 30s elapse or earlier if the stay-awake process exits, its stdin is closed, or it receives SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGINT.
Returns: no output on success.
